title: Quantum Online Encryption Against Ideal Online Modes
summary: No online mode, including QCB, can achieve qIND-qCPA under a random-permutation comparison; defining and proving security against an ideal online mode remains open.

formal_statement.body: For QCB, an online authenticated-encryption mode, the $\mathrm{qIND\text{-}qCPA}$ security definition cannot be achieved by any online mode, including QCB, when security is formulated by distinguishing the mode from a random-permutation idealization. An attack causing this limitation should no longer apply if the comparison target is changed to an ideal online mode. The unresolved task is therefore to define a security notion for a quantum-secure online encryption mode in which an adversary distinguishes the mode from an ideal online mode rather than from a random permutation, and to analyze that notion by giving security definitions and proofs. Determine whether such a notion can be formulated and establish corresponding security results for online modes; the resulting definitions and security proofs may be substantially more involved than those for the random-permutation comparison.

scope.domain: Quantum-secure online authenticated encryption and distinguishing-based security definitions.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Formulate a security notion comparing a quantum-secure online mode with an ideal online mode and establish corresponding definitions, proofs, and security results.

progress.summary: The source presents comparison with an ideal online mode as a way the stated attack should no longer apply. It explicitly leaves formulation of the definition and its security proofs as an open problem.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., QCB: Efficient Quantum-secure Authenticated Encryption
